question: What does a PET scan primarily measure within the human body?
explanation: PET scans track metabolic and biochemical processes by following radiopharmaceuticals in living tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h1)

question: How do PET scans differ from standard CT scans?

options.A: PET requires permanent surgical implantation of tracers
options.B: PET shows body function while CT shows body structure
options.C: PET takes less than five seconds to capture whole bodies
options.D: PET uses high-voltage sound waves instead of radiation

explanation: Standard imaging visualizes anatomy, whereas nuclear medicine highlights functional changes in cells. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which radiopharmaceutical is most commonly used in routine clinical PET scans?
explanation: FDG mimics glucose and is taken up heavily by metabolically active cells. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h2)

question: A patient asks why they must rest quietly after receiving their FDG injection. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: To lower your blood pressure before entering the cold imaging room
options.B: To keep your heart rate high enough for the scanner to detect blood flow
options.C: To allow the radioactive dye to completely leave your body through sweat
options.D: To prevent muscles from taking up the sugar tracer instead of target cells

explanation: Muscle movement increases glucose consumption, which creates unwanted background noise on the scan. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h2)

question: In which clinical area is PET imaging most frequently utilized?
explanation: Oncology uses PET extensively to detect malignant growths and monitor therapy success. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why would a cardiologist order a PET scan for a patient with heart failure?

options.A: To view the physical size of heart valve calcifications
options.B: To check if damaged heart muscle is still alive and salvageable
options.C: To clear blood clots completely out of the coronary arteries
options.D: To measure the exact electrical conduction speed of the ventricles

explanation: Cardiac PET assesses myocardial viability to see if blood flow restoration will improve heart function. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h3)

question: How many hours of fasting are typically required before an FDG-PET scan?
explanation: Short-term fasting helps lower baseline blood glucose levels so the radiotracer is absorbed properly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the primary reason high blood sugar ruins an FDG-PET scan?

options.A: Elevated blood glucose makes the patient too weak to lie flat
options.B: Sugar neutralizes the radioactive decay particles inside the veins
options.C: Excess sugar competes with the radioactive tracer for cell uptake
options.D: High glucose levels cause the scanner cameras to overheat instantly

explanation: When too much normal glucose is present, cells ignore the FDG tracer, ruining the image contrast. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why must the patient empty their bladder right before the scanning phase begins?

options.A: To reduce pelvic radiation exposure and prevent image artifacts
options.B: To measure accurate fluid balance output during the procedure
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling dizzy during the rapid spin
options.D: To test the urine sample for hidden infectious bacteria

explanation: An empty bladder limits radiation pooling near pelvic organs and stops movement caused by discomfort. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the main nursing goal during the tracer uptake waiting period?

options.A: Encouraging light exercises to speed up tracer distribution
options.B: Promoting absolute physical rest and reducing anxiety
options.C: Performing complete neurological assessments every five minutes
options.D: Administering large volumes of intravenous electrolyte fluids

explanation: Rest prevents muscles from taking up glucose, ensuring the tracer reaches targeted pathological tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the most effective way for a patient to clear remaining tracers after a PET scan?

options.A: Taking strong laxatives to clean out the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Undergoing whole-body therapeutic massage sessions daily
options.C: Drinking plenty of fluids and urinating frequently
options.D: Breathing pure oxygen through a tight facial mask

explanation: Hydration and urination help eliminate the remaining water-soluble radioactive isotopes safely. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h6)

question: A patient who just completed a PET scan wants to hold their newborn grandchild immediately. What instruction should the nurse give?

options.A: There are no restrictions because the radiation disappears instantly
options.B: Limit close contact with infants for the rest of the day as a precaution
options.C: Wait exactly two full weeks before being in the same room with children
options.D: Wash the baby thoroughly with antiseptic soap after the visit

explanation: Minimizing close exposure to vulnerable groups for several hours protects them from residual radiation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h6)
